question: If each observation is halved then the coefficient of quartile deviation
solution:
The correct answer is that it remains same.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

**Calculation: **The formulae we need for solving the problem are as follows: 

mathbf{{Quartile formula for Q1,grouped data}}=Q₁=I₁+((N/4)-c)/(f)*(I₂-I₁)\\mathbf{{Quartile formula for Q3,grouped data}}=Q₃=I₁+(3*(N/4)-c)/(f)*(I₂-I₁)\ mathbf{{Coefficient of quartile deviation}}=frac{Q₃-Q₁}{Q₃+Q₁} 

Here, since all the observations are doubled the value for Quartiles becomes:

{Quartile formula for Q1,grouped data}=Q₁=I₁+((frac{1)/(2)N/4)- (1)/(2)c}{(1)/(2)f}*(I₂-I₁)\\implies{Quartile formula for Q1,grouped data}=Q₁=I₁+((N/4)-c)/(f)*(I₂-I₁)\{Quartile formula for Q3,grouped data}=Q₃=I₁+(3*(frac{1)/(2)N/4)-(1)/(2)c}{(1)/(2)f}*(I₂-I₁) \\implies{Quartile formula for Q3,grouped data}=Q₃=I₁+(3*(N/4)-c)/(f)*(I₂-I₁)\ {Coefficient of quartile deviation}=frac{Q₃-Q₁}{Q₃+Q₁} 

This is the same value as the coefficient of quartile deviation when the values of the observation of the data set were unchanged.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The formula in this case used is for grouped data as well.
 
• The same result can be derived for ungrouped data as well.

**Hence, if each observation is halved then the coefficient of quartile deviation remains same. **
